title: The Four Forces of Flight
seo_title: Grade 6 Science: The Four Forces of Flight Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Identify the four forces of flight (lift, weight, thrust and drag); explain how Bernoulli's principle and wing shape produce lift; describe how changing the forces changes an aircraft's motion. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand D: Structures and Mechanisms – Flight)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 science worksheets on lift, weight, thrust and drag, Bernoulli's principle, wing shape, control surfaces and streamlining. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Lift, weight, thrust and drag act on a plane.
key_sub: Lift beats weight to rise; thrust beats drag to speed up; balanced forces mean steady flight.
body_html:
How to think about it

Four forces act on anything that flies.

  • Lift pushes up and weight (gravity) pulls down. Thrust pushes forward and drag pulls back.
  • Bernoulli's principle: faster air has lower pressure. A curved wing (airfoil) makes faster air over the top, giving lift.
  • Rudder, elevators and ailerons steer the plane. Streamlined shapes reduce drag.
Example

Lift is 80 kN and weight is 60 kN. What happens?

lift is bigger

Answer: the plane climbs

Example

Which force does a jet engine make?

it pushes the plane forward

Answer: thrust

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up thrust and lift.
  • Thinking planes need no lift once they are moving.
  • Thinking drag only acts on slow planes.

faq.q: What are the four forces of flight?
How does a wing make lift?
faq.a: The curved wing makes air move faster over the top, so pressure above is lower than below, and the wing is pushed up.
A smooth, pointed shape reduces drag, so the plane uses less fuel.

items.q: What is Bernoulli's principle about?
items.e: Wings make air move faster over the top.

items.q: Why do jet engines push air backward?
c: Pushing air back pushes the plane forward (action and reaction).
items.e: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction.

items.q: Which of the four forces of flight comes from the engines of a jet?
items.e: That force is thrust.

items.q: Which of the four forces of flight increases when a plane flies faster through the air?
items.e: That force is drag.

items.q: Which of the four forces of flight pushes the plane up, made by air moving over the wings?
items.e: That force is lift.

items.q: An airplane is flying level at a steady speed. What is true about the forces?
items.e: Balanced forces mean no change in motion.

items.q: Why is the air harder to fly in high up in the mountains?
c: The air is thinner, so wings make less lift.
items.e: Fewer air particles push on the wing.

items.q: Which of the four forces of flight acts against lift?
items.e: That force is weight (gravity).

items.q: Why is the top of a wing curved?
c: Air moves faster over the top, making lower pressure above the wing, which gives lift.
items.e: This wing shape is an airfoil.

items.q: What is a fair test for paper airplane designs?
c: use different paper for each and guess
throw each one with the same force from the same height and measure the distance
items.e: Change one variable at a time.

items.q: What does the rudder on the tail control?
c: turning the nose left or right (yaw)
items.e: The rudder moves side to side.

items.q: Which of the four forces of flight pushes the plane forward, made by the engines or propeller?
items.e: That force is thrust.

items.q: What do the elevators on the tail control?
c: the nose moving up or down (pitch)
items.e: Elevators tilt the plane up or down.

items.q: Which of the four forces of flight is made when a wing is tilted up slightly into the air (angle of attack)?
items.e: That force is lift.

items.q: Which of the four forces of flight acts against weight?
items.e: That force is lift.

items.q: Which of the four forces of flight acts against thrust?
items.e: That force is drag.

items.q: Which of the four forces of flight acts against drag?
items.e: That force is thrust.

items.q: Paper airplane A has wide wings. Paper airplane B has narrow wings. Both have the same mass. Which likely glides further?
c: B, because narrow wings make more lift
A, because wide wings make more lift
items.e: Wing area affects lift.

items.q: Which of the four forces of flight grows when more passengers and bags are loaded?
items.e: That force is weight (gravity).

items.q: Which force must a parachute increase to slow a skydiver?
items.e: A large canopy catches lots of air.

items.q: Why do skydivers' speeds stop increasing after a while?

items.q: Why might a parachute investigation give different times for the same parachute?

items.q: Why does a parachute slow a skydiver down?
c: Its large area causes lots of air resistance.
items.e: More area, more resistance.

items.q: Why do many sea animals have similar streamlined shapes?
